text: Clinton Conger Ballard Jr. (May 24, 1931 – December 23, 2008) was an American songwriter, singer, and pianist who wrote two Billboard Hot 100 number one hits. The first was "Game of Love" by Wayne Fontana and The Mindbenders in 1965, which reached number one in the US and peaked at number two in the UK. The second was "You're No Good," a 1975 hit by Linda Ronstadt, first sung by Dee Dee Warwick, covered by The Swinging Blue Jeans, Betty Everett, and later recorded by Van Halen; Betty Everett's version reached the Top Ten of the US Billboard R&B chart, while the Linda Ronstadt version reached number one on the Billboard chart. He also wrote two UK number one singles: "Good Timin'" by Jimmy Jones in 1960 and "I'm Alive" by The Hollies in 1965. When Ballard was three, he played the piano for KTSM, an El Paso radio station; at age 11, he attended a musical program for gifted students at the University of North Texas. After serving in the US Army, he moved to New York and became a songwriter and composer, including of the musical *Come Back Little Sheba*. His song "Hey, Little Baby" was recorded by Mitch Miller and became the theme for the 1958 World's Fair in Belgium. In 1957, he discovered the Kalin Twins and became their manager, writing their Decca debut single "Jumpin' Jack," which was followed by "When," a US Top Ten hit and number one on the UK Singles Chart. After leaving the Kalins in 1958, he wrote "Ev'ry Hour, Ev'ry Day of My Life" for Malcolm Vaughan and "Ginger Bread" for Frankie Avalon, the latter a Top Ten hit. His own recording career was less successful; in 1960, he adopted the pseudonym Buddy Clinton to record a two-sided single featuring "Take Me to Your Ladder (I'll See Your Leader Later)" and "Joanie's Forever," both co-written by Burt Bacharach and Bob Hilliard. In 1963, he wrote "You're No Good," first recorded by Dee Dee Warwick, with Betty Everett's version reaching the US Billboard R&B Top Ten; The Swinging Blue Jeans also recorded it in 1966. His songs were frequently recorded by British Invasion artists: The Swinging Blue Jeans recorded "It Isn't There," the Zombies recorded "Gotta Get a Hold of Myself" in 1966, and The Hollies recorded "I'm Alive," which reached number one in the UK in 1965. He also wrote "The Game of Love" for Wayne Fontana and The Mindbenders in 1965, as well as their subsequent chart singles "It's Just a Little Bit Too Late" and "She Needs Love." Ballard wrote songs for the Ricky Nelson film *Love and Kisses* and composed a series of commercial jingles, including a theme for Greyhound Lines. He died in Denton, Texas, in December 2008, two years after suffering a stroke. He is not to be confused with fellow songwriters Russ Ballard, Glen Ballard, or Hank Ballard.
